html:
The Ninam, or Yanam, are one of the subgroups of the Yanomami peoples, living in the upper Mucajaí and Uraricoera river basins of Roraima, in northern Brazil, and across the border in Venezuela. They speak Ninam, one of the Yanomaman languages.

They live in communal houses in the forest, farming plantains and manioc and hunting. In the late 1980s gold miners invaded Yanomami lands in Roraima, bringing malaria and violence. The Yanomami Indigenous Territory was created in 1992, but illegal mining has returned many times since. Neighbours: Macuxi and Wapishana.
